--- page 6 ---
Figure 1: Somalia crisis timeline (FSNAU initial draft, Feb 2020) for a projected poor Gu (long) rains. Gantt-style heatmap, months Jan-Dec on x, ~21 impact pathways on y, red intensity = severity build-up. Key timings: livestock pasture/water scarcity May-Oct; abnormal livestock migration from May (intense May-Jul); poor body condition, low goat/sheep prices May-Oct; low livestock conception Apr-Jun; low births Oct-Dec; milk production poor Jun-Dec; livestock deaths Aug-Sep; crop cultivation low Mar-May; low agri labour Mar-Jul; failed cereal harvest Jul-Aug; market low stock/high prices Jun-Dec (peak Oct-Nov); displacement from drought areas Jun-Aug; malnutrition admissions Jun-Oct; water low availability May-Oct; water price Apr-Dec (peak Sep-Oct); measles and AWD/cholera rows have no shading; education (school dropout) May-Aug. Text: cholera outbreaks 2-3 weeks after water dries, measles after 3-4 months.
--- page 7 ---
narrative text, no figure. Section 3 Forecast and Triggers: AA financing triggered by risk of out-of-the-ordinary crisis like 2010/11 (famine) and 2016/17 (near famine); food security forecasts as proxy. Forecast source: FSNAU + FEWS NET quarterly IPC projections. TRIGGER (start): finance triggered if projected population in IPC Phase 3+ exceeds 20% AND projected Phase 3 population increases by a further 5%, OR (see next page).
--- page 8 ---
narrative text, no figure. Third trigger criterion: projected population in IPC Phase 4+ is 2.5% (fail-safe). Roles: FSNAU alerts HC when trigger reached; HC/OCHA CO notifies OCHA HQ; HCT and ICCG alerted. Section 4 start: actions that prevent/mitigate impact (risk communication; water points rehab).
--- page 9 ---
narrative text, no figure (mitigation: clean water, drought-tolerant seeds/FAW control, livestock treatment+feed; protect: cash transfers scaled horizontally/vertically to stop IPC2 districts slipping to 3-4).
--- page 10 ---
Diagram: "Somalia Anticipatory Action Plan" - MITIGATE (sustain food production, livestock production, sustain water supply) | centre: Inform, empower & engage / Communication with affected people | PROTECT (sustain purchasing power, keep children in school, prevent disease outbreaks and malnutrition); base: Centrality of protection. Text: rapid response teams for outbreaks, school feeding, blanket feeding.
--- page 11 ---
Table (summary of interventions: cluster/action/agency/caseload/lead time/cost). FOOD SECURITY (FAO, WFP): drought-smart farming ~40,000 households, 45 days (south central) / 90 days (northwest), ~USD 270-330/hh; FAW/pest control 75 days, ~USD 60,000/district; desert locust 60 days, ~USD 33/ha; livestock treatment up to 14.7M animals, 60-75 days, ~USD 0.40/animal; supplementary feeds 120 days, ~USD 110/hh; unconditional cash (FAO&WFP) 30-90 days; conditional cash 60-105 days; both cost = Minimum Expenditure Basket value. WASH (UNICEF, IOM): borehole rehab 600,000 people, 4 weeks, 7,200,000; new boreholes 250,000 people, 4-6 weeks, 20,000,000.
--- page 12 ---
Table cont. WASH: shallow wells 400,000 people, 2-4 weeks, 3,600,000; sub-surface water extraction in dried riverbeds 300,000, 3 months, 3,600,000; AWD prevention 2,700,000 people in hotspots, 1 month, 13,050,000. EDUCATION (UNICEF): school feeding 338,773 children, 1.5 months, USD 7/child/month x 6 = USD 42; water for school children USD 3.96/child; teacher incentives 8,469 teachers, USD 100/month; child protection services USD 381,060 total (USD 4.1/child). NUTRITION (WFP): BSFP children U2 90,948, 1 month, 3,154,077; micro-nutrient suppl. PLW 30,943, 2,231,609.
--- page 13 ---
Table cont. NUTRITION (UNICEF): micronutrient tabs PLW 282,571, 729,881; MNP children U2 334,911, 612,887. HEALTH (WHO), each targeting ~1/3 of Somalia's districts, ~5,000,000 people, one month: PHEOCs/Rapid Response Teams $1,650,000; EWARN scale-up $735,000; laboratory capacity $250,000.
--- page 14 ---
Table cont. HEALTH (WHO): risk communication $280,000; infection prevention & control $1,400,000. UNICEF emergency lifesaving healthcare: 300,000 people in IPC 3-4 areas, 2-4 weeks, 3,097,347. PROTECTION (UNHCR): monitoring in 40 districts for 3 months, 300,000 USD, 2 weeks, FSNAU caseload.
--- page 15 ---
Table cont. RISK COMMUNICATION (UNICEF/OCHA/clusters), 60 days: community-level risk comms $459,200 ($80k printing, $150k training, $152k monitoring, $105k surge); media campaign $180,000. Scenarios: worst case 30 affected districts ~3.5M pop; moderate 15 districts ~1.75M; optimistic 5 districts ~0.58M. Then intro to calendar of actions.

--- page 22 ---
Annex I conceptual graphics: (1) traditional humanitarian response: Severe Crisis -> assessing needs -> planning/prioritizing -> mobilizing/allocating funding -> aid delivery; (2) collective AA: robust forecasting & decision-making framework + established action plans + pre-arranged financing -> Anticipatory Action -> reduced crisis; (3) rationale: reduce humanitarian impact and response cost; more dignified; protect development gains; (4) impact-reduction curve: earlier AA flattens the impact curve vs later traditional response.
--- page 23 ---
Annex II table: full list of drought anticipatory actions by cluster/agency: Food Security (FAO; FAO&WFP for cash), WASH (UNICEF, IOM), Education (UNICEF), Nutrition (WFP; UNICEF), Health (WHO; UNICEF), Protection (UNHCR), Risk Communication (UNICEF/OCHA/all clusters). 23 actions in total; same as the summary table, no numbers.
--- page 24 ---
Annex III CERF finance release process (text): Step 1 trigger validation, 1 day, RC/HC decides, OCHA supports (is data in conflict with forecast? is trigger mainly drought?); Step 2 rapid analysis of projected impact, 2 days, RC/HC leads (scope, cost, readiness, access); RC/HC informs ERC who decides CERF envelope; Step 3 re-calibration of AA plan (start).
--- page 25 ---
Annex III cont.: Step 3 re-calibration, 1-2 days (prioritize activities/locations, minimal plan changes, allocate envelope, choose organizations); Step 4 preparation and submission of CERF application, 5 days (OCHA compiles, HC submits to CERF secretariat, AA plan annexed); Step 5 due diligence and disbursement approval, 4 days. Total indicative about 13-14 days. Optional OCHA advocacy, links to World Bank/Start Fund/DREF, evaluation.
